name: project-git
description: How git works in an Archon Horizon workspace — one out-of-tree workspace ledger (no per-project repos); read a project's history by pathspec or by a session's commit trailers.
---

Read this before running `git diff`/`git log` on a project.

## The model

- **One out-of-tree workspace ledger.** Archon commits to a single repo whose git
  dir is `.archon-horizon/vcs/workspace.git` with the workspace **root** as its
  work tree (driven via `--git-dir`/`--work-tree`). `<root>/.git` is deliberately
  untouched — it is reserved for a user repo. The ledger records one commit per
  completed session: `config.yaml`, the session's scoped project files, and
  `.archon-horizon/` shared state; never the binary git dirs under
  `.archon-horizon/vcs/`, locks, or other volatile internals.
- **There are no per-project repositories.** A project directory has no nested
  `.git/`, and there is no `.archon-horizon/vcs/<project>.git`. A project's
  "history" is simply the workspace ledger filtered to that project's path.
- **You record your own work by committing to the ledger** with plain `git` (see
  below). Commit *early and often* with a semantic, math-first message — the
  commit message + diff is how your progress is read, so make the message say what
  you proved/built. Provenance trailers are added automatically; do not write them.

So a plain `git diff` at the root sees only a user repo (if any), never Archon's.
Drive the out-of-tree workspace ledger explicitly (or use `hgit`).

## Recording your work (committing)

Commits go to the ledger, **not** to `<root>/.git` and **not** via any project
`.git` (there is none). Do **not** `export GIT_DIR` / `GIT_WORK_TREE` yourself — that
would redirect `lake` and other tooling. Two equivalent ways to commit:

```bash
# 1) The `hgit` wrapper (on the session env as $HORIZON_GIT) — plain git, ledger-scoped:
"$HORIZON_GIT" add path/to/File.lean
"$HORIZON_GIT" commit -m "feat(chapter): prove foo_lemma" \
  --trailer 'Summary=**Proof.** Closed the compactness step using $K \subseteq X$.'

# 2) The explicit form (identical effect):
git --git-dir="$HORIZON_LEDGER_GIT_DIR" --work-tree="$HORIZON_LEDGER_WORK_TREE" \
    add path/to/File.lean
git --git-dir="$HORIZON_LEDGER_GIT_DIR" --work-tree="$HORIZON_LEDGER_WORK_TREE" \
    commit -m "feat(chapter): prove foo_lemma" \
    --trailer 'Summary=**Proof.** Closed the compactness step using $K \subseteq X$.'
```

Ordinary git: the ledger's index tracks HEAD, so `add` then `commit` records your
files on top of it. Horizon's own commits stage in a private index and never leave
anything staged in your way.

- **Prefer the pathspec commit** — name the paths on the commit itself:
  `"$HORIZON_GIT" commit -m "…" --trailer 'Summary=…' -- path/to/File.lean`
  It records exactly those files, ignores whatever else may be staged, and git
  builds its tree from the **current** HEAD — so it cannot silently revert a
  concurrent session's files the way a commit built on a stale index can.
- Add at least one **`Summary` trailer** explaining the important change, not
  merely repeating the subject. Use one trailer per distinct explanation when
  useful. Its value supports Markdown and LaTeX, so concise mathematical context
  such as `--trailer 'Summary=**Invariant.** Preserves $f(x)=x$ on $A$.'` renders

176	`FinCoverData.flat_sections_pieces`, which localized a FREE pinned-chart ring; here it is the
177	flat structure morphism of the relative curve read on an affine open. -/

187	    Module.Flat R Γ(relCurve C R, D.pieces i ⊓ D.pieces j) :=
188	  flat_sections_isAffineOpen C R hinf

195	Θ-layer (it agrees with `relPinnedChart` by `rfl`). -/

200	pinned `P¹` charts, containing it.  This is what the Θ-twisting unit genuinely needs (the
201	theta cocycle lives on `V₀ ⊓ V₁`), and it is deliberately a SEPARATE datum: no certificate
202	clause and no locally-certified predicate may require it.  Keeping it separate is what stops

204	structure ChartTyping [IsAffineHom π] (D : AffCoverData C R) where
205	  /-- Which pinned chart the piece is assigned to. -/
206	  side : D.index → Bool
207	  /-- The piece is contained in its assigned chart. -/
208	  piece_le : ∀ j, D.pieces j ≤ pinnedChartOfSide C R π (side j)

214	variable {C R π} [IsAffineHom π] (D : FinCoverData C R π)
215	
216	/-- **The migration map.** An old chart-typed `FinCoverData` gives a widened
217	`AffCoverData`: reindex `Fin m₀ ⊕ Fin m₁` through `finSumFinEquiv`, the pieces are affine as
218	basic opens of the affine pinned charts, and the joint cover follows from the two chart-wise
219	covers together with `relCover_sup`.
220	
221	The point of this lemma is that widening costs nothing landed: every existing construction of
222	cover data still produces a legal widened datum.  The converse fails, and that is exactly the
223	content of R2. -/

225	  m := D.m₀ + D.m₁
226	  pieces := fun j => D.pieces (finSumFinEquiv.symm j)
227	  isAffineOpen := fun j => by
228	    rcases finSumFinEquiv.symm j with i | i
229	    · rw [FinCoverData.pieces_inl]
230	      exact (relCover_isAffineOpen₀ C R (fiberTwoCover π)).basicOpen _
231	    · rw [FinCoverData.pieces_inr]
232	      exact (relCover_isAffineOpen₁ C R (fiberTwoCover π)).basicOpen _
233	  cover := by
234	    refine top_le_iff.mp fun z _ => ?_
235	    -- every point is in a pinned chart, and each chart is covered by its own pieces
236	    have hz : z ∈ (relCover C R (fiberTwoCover π)).V₀
237	        ⊔ (relCover C R (fiberTwoCover π)).V₁ := by
238	      rw [relCover_sup]; trivial
239	    have key : ∃ i : D.index, z ∈ D.pieces i := by
240	      rcases Opens.mem_sup.mp hz with h | h
241	      · obtain ⟨i, hi⟩ := Opens.mem_iSup.mp (D.cover₀ h)
242	        exact ⟨Sum.inl i, hi⟩
243	      · obtain ⟨i, hi⟩ := Opens.mem_iSup.mp (D.cover₁ h)
244	        exact ⟨Sum.inr i, hi⟩
245	    obtain ⟨i, hi⟩ := key
246	    exact Opens.mem_iSup.mpr ⟨finSumFinEquiv i, by
247	      simpa only [Equiv.symm_apply_apply] using hi⟩

250	lemma toAffCoverData_pieces (j : Fin (D.m₀ + D.m₁)) :
251	    D.toAffCoverData.pieces j = D.pieces (finSumFinEquiv.symm j) := rfl
252

254	chart-1 pieces of `V₁`. -/

256	  side := fun j => (finSumFinEquiv.symm j).isRight
257	  piece_le := fun j => by
258	    rw [toAffCoverData_pieces]
259	    rcases h : finSumFinEquiv.symm j with i | i
260	    · rw [FinCoverData.pieces_inl]
261	      exact (relCurve C R).basicOpen_le (D.h₀ i)
262	    · rw [FinCoverData.pieces_inr]
263	      exact (relCurve C R).basicOpen_le (D.h₁ i)

9	# The chart-typed → widened comparison (R2, human decision I-0492)
10	
11	The widened lane (`DivisorFamilyAff*.lean`) is worth nothing to the DD-R chain until every
12	certificate the chart-typed design already produced instantiates it.  That is this file: the
13	migration of a `DivisorAdaptation` (over a `FinCoverData`, i.e. basic opens of the two pinned
14	`P¹` charts) to an `AffAdaptation` over the widened cover `FinCoverData.toAffCoverData`,
15	CERTIFICATE INCLUDED, and the induced map `DivFamZar → DivFamZarAff`.
16	
17	## Why it is nearly free, and where the one real step is
18	
19	`toAffCoverData.pieces j` is *definitionally* `D.pieces (finSumFinEquiv.symm j)`, so the
20	section rings, the equations, the colength modules, the overlap ideals and both overlap arrows
21	are the ORIGINAL ones read at a relabelled index — every comparison below that looks like it
22	needs a transport is `rfl`.  Clauses (c1) therefore transport pointwise.
23	
24	The one real step is the glued clauses (c2)/(c3)/(c4): `gluedSubmodule` is a kernel inside
25	`∀ j : index, colength j`, so it must be carried along the index equivalence.  The transport
26	is `LinearEquiv.piCongrLeft`, used in the `symm` direction because that direction evaluates
27	CAST-FREE (`(piCongrLeft φ e).symm g j = g (e j)`), which is what keeps the intertwining
28	proofs from drowning in `Eq.mpr`s.
29	
30	## Main declarations
31	
32	* `AlgebraicGeometry.DivisorAdaptation.toAff` — the widened adaptation of a chart-typed one.
33	* `DivisorAdaptation.gluedCongr` — the glued modules agree, along `piCongrLeft.symm`.
34	* `DivisorAdaptation.isCertified_toAff` — the certificate migrates, all seven clauses.
35	* `AlgebraicGeometry.CertifiedDivisorFamily.toAff` — the certified family migrates.
36	* `AlgebraicGeometry.isLocallyCertifiedAff_of_isLocallyCertified` — the chart-typed pin
37	  implies the widened one.
38	* `AlgebraicGeometry.DivFamZar.toAff` — the induced map of functor values, compatible with
39	  `picClass`.
40	-/

11	
12	The corrected cert-collapse claim (roadmap `...certificate.cert-collapse`, as amended after
13	the I-0340 refutation), carried out on the widened cover.
14	
15	## What was refuted and what survives
16	
17	The refuted claim was that (c2)/(c3)/(c4) are FREE for a swallow-or-miss adaptation.  They are
18	not, and `DivisorFamilyAffCollapse.lean` kernel-checks why: `toOvlLeft i i = toOvlRight i i`
19	by `rfl`, so every diagonal component of `deltaLeft - deltaRight` vanishes for EVERY
20	adaptation, and the diagonal factor always survives in the cokernel.  Clause (c4) therefore
21	always implies flatness of the diagonal overlap colengths — no structural observation about
22	which pieces meet the support can remove that.
23	
24	What survives is the REDUCTION the amended node states: on a cover with a straddling piece,
25	(c2)/(c3)/(c4) follow from (c1)-projectivity alone.  This file proves it.
26	
27	## The mechanism, and it is sharper than the node's account
28	
29	With a straddling piece `j₀`, every OTHER piece misses the support, so
30	`subsingleton_ovlColength_of_disjoint` kills every overlap colength that involves an index
31	`≠ j₀` — in particular every OFF-DIAGONAL one, since a pair `(i, j)` with `i ≠ j` has at least
32	one entry `≠ j₀`.  Combined with the vanishing diagonal, `deltaLeft - deltaRight` is the ZERO
33	map (`deltaSub_eq_zero_of_swallowedBy`).  Hence:
34	
35	* `gluedSubmodule = ⊤`, so `Glued ≃ chartProd` — (c2) becomes a statement about the product of
36	  the piece colengths, of which all but one are subsingleton;
37	* `chartProd ⧸ gluedSubmodule` is subsingleton, so (c3) is free — and this IS free, with no
38	  input, which is the one part of the original claim that was right;
39	* `range (deltaLeft - deltaRight) = ⊥`, so the (c4) cokernel is `ovlProd` itself, whose
40	  factors are the overlap colengths: all subsingleton except `ovlColength j₀ j₀`.  So (c4)
41	  reduces to flatness of THAT ONE module — exactly the residue the refutation predicted, now
42	  isolated to a single index instead of a whole cover.
